title: PostgresAI vs Netdata: wait events and experts vs per-second metrics
description: Netdata collects per-second PostgreSQL metrics with built-in alerts and ML anomaly scores. PostgresAI adds a wait event dashboard, Issues with a fix and experts on Scale.
summary: Netdata is a monitoring tool with a PostgreSQL collector: the open-source Agent collects Postgres metrics every second, ships 14 built-in PostgreSQL alerts and scores every metric for anomalies with ML. Per-query data comes from Top Queries and Running Queries functions that need Netdata Cloud. PostgresAI monitors only PostgreSQL, runs scheduled checkups and turns findings into Issues that you, your AI agent or a PostgresAI expert can act on. Pick Netdata for per-second Postgres metrics and anomaly detection on a free tier. Pick PostgresAI for per-query dashboards, a sampled history of wait events, checkups and human experts. The two can run side by side.
chooseThem: The PostgreSQL collector gathers server, database, table and index metrics every second by default, including replication lag, WAL archiving, checkpoints, locks, bloat and unused indexes.
ML anomaly detection runs on each Agent with 18 models per metric, Postgres metrics included; Netdata documents a cost of 2-4% of one CPU for 10,000 metrics.
The collector needs a user with the pg_monitor role and ships 14 alerts, including transaction ID exhaustion, table and index bloat and time since last autovacuum.
Top Queries prefers pg_stat_monitor when installed, adding application name, client IP, CPU time and errors per query to the pg_stat_statements columns.
The Agent is open source under GPL v3+ with a built-in MCP server from v2.6.0; a free Community plan covers up to 5 nodes, and Business is from $7 per node a month on annual billing.

proofs.them: Netdata keeps metrics and logs on your nodes and sends hostnames, metric names and alerts to Netdata Cloud. Its docs note that Top Queries text may contain unmasked literal values, and Running Queries shows the SQL being executed.

Netdata's Running Queries function, which requires Netdata Cloud, shows live snapshots of active sessions from pg_stat_activity with their wait events. The collector charts connections and locks. The sources we reviewed do not describe a history of sampled wait events.

Netdata Business includes email and ticket support in business hours with an SLA, and Enterprise offers 24/7 support with a dedicated team. The sources we reviewed do not describe PostgreSQL expert help.

rows.them: A monitoring tool with a PostgreSQL collector. The open-source Agent collects metrics every second on each node, keeps them locally, scores them for anomalies and evaluates alerts; Netdata Cloud adds a central view.

The PostgreSQL collector connects by DSN to local or remote servers and documents Azure Database for PostgreSQL examples with Azure AD authentication. A separate Amazon RDS collector reads metrics from rds_exporter every 10 seconds; its page does not name PostgreSQL. The sources we reviewed do not mention Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, Aurora or Google Cloud SQL by name.

The Agent runs on your own servers and keeps metrics and logs there; Netdata Cloud receives metadata such as hostnames, metric names and alerts. Netdata Cloud On-Prem, on Kubernetes, puts the control plane in your environment and comes with the Enterprise plan.

The Agent is open source under GPL v3 or later. The dashboard UI is closed source and free to use with the Agent and Cloud under the NCUL1 license. Netdata Cloud has paid plans above the free Community plan.

A Top Queries function reads pg_stat_monitor or pg_stat_statements and shows calls, total and mean time, rows and block and temp I/O per query; Running Queries lists current queries from pg_stat_activity. Both require Netdata Cloud. The sources we reviewed do not describe per-query metric charts in the collector.

Running Queries, which requires Netdata Cloud, lists current sessions from pg_stat_activity with each one's wait event and wait event type. The collector charts connections and locks. The sources we reviewed do not describe a history of sampled wait events.

14 built-in PostgreSQL alerts cover connection and lock utilization, transaction ID exhaustion, cache hit ratios, rollback ratio, deadlocks, table and index bloat and time since last autovacuum and autoanalyze. The sources we reviewed do not describe recommendations or reports.

Every Agent and Parent from v2.6.0 has a built-in MCP server, and Netdata Cloud has one MCP endpoint for all nodes on paid plans. It covers metric, alert and function discovery, metric queries and alert history; setup guides cover Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI and VS Code.
Not documented in the sources we reviewed. The PostgreSQL collector reads statistics; the sources do not describe trying a change on a copy of the data.

Business includes email and ticket support in business hours with an SLA; Enterprise offers 24/7 support with a dedicated team and priority support plans. The sources we reviewed do not describe PostgreSQL consulting.
Alerts are evaluated on each Agent, with a central alert view in Netdata Cloud. On the free Community plan, notifications go to Discord, email and the mobile app.

On the Agent, in three tiers by default: per-second for 14 days, per-minute for 3 months and per-hour for 2 years, each capped at 1 GiB, whichever limit comes first. Limits are configurable, and Netdata charges no retention fee.
Netdata states SOC 2 Type 2 compliance for the Security, Availability and Confidentiality criteria, and that it is not PCI DSS or HIPAA certified.

pricing.notes: Open source, GPL v3+; dashboard UI closed source, free to use
Netdata Cloud for up to 5 connected nodes, 1 custom dashboard per room; no MCP server, AI Investigations or on-premise

Infrastructure, billed annually, or $8.75 with monthly billing; unlimited nodes, retention and custom dashboards, AI conversations (fair use), RBAC, SSO, SCIM, Netdata Cloud MCP server, business-hours support with SLA; 14-day trial
Everything in Business, on-premise deployment at any size, custom pricing above 500 nodes, priority support plans

pricingNote: Optional products, including AI Investigations, are billed separately. Metrics stay on your infrastructure, so storage costs for longer retention are yours.
together: Netdata collects per-second PostgreSQL metrics and scores them for anomalies; PostgresAI monitoring adds per-query dashboards, a sampled history of wait events, checkups and Issues. They collect separately, so a team can run both.

faq.a: The Netdata Agent is open source under GPL v3 or later. The dashboard UI is closed source but free to use with the Agent and Cloud. Netdata Cloud has a free Community plan and paid plans.

Partly. Its PostgreSQL collector charts server, database, table and index metrics every second and ships 14 alerts. A Top Queries function reads pg_stat_statements or pg_stat_monitor, and a Running Queries function reads pg_stat_activity; both require Netdata Cloud.

The Agent is free. Netdata Cloud Community is $0 for up to 5 nodes. Business starts at $7 per node a month with annual billing, or $8.75 with monthly billing. Enterprise, including on-premise deployment, has custom pricing.

faq.q: Can I use PostgresAI and Netdata together?
faq.a: Yes. Netdata collects per-second PostgreSQL metrics and alerts, and PostgresAI monitoring adds per-query dashboards, a sampled history of wait events, checkups and Issues. They collect separately.
